why: Readers: the form is not named and a direct question is polite too. That is the rule (3 and 21 November: give the situation, the check looks for the form), as r21b-1-038 and r21c-006 decided. Checks tested: natural answers pass (Could you tell me / Can you / Would you mind telling me / Do you know / I'd like to know / I was wondering + when / what date / if + statement order, also 'will start', 'is going to start'); 'when does the course start', 'when starts the course', 'when will the course start', 'when is the start date' and a bare direct question fail.

Same reader flag as 001, decided by the rule (situation, not the form named; r21c-007). Checks tested: 'if you have sent / if you sent / whether my printer has been sent / when my printer will arrive / where my order is / why it hasn't arrived / what happened to my order' pass; 'if did you send', 'when will my printer arrive', 'where is my order', 'if have you sent', 'when arrives my printer', 'why hasn't my printer arrived' fail.

Both readers confirm 'it expand' is a believable B1 mistake (the zero-conditional card's own mistake type, r21c-008). The three right sentences share the pattern because that is the topic, but they are about three different things (bus travel, saving work, reading glasses) and none is a near-copy of the wrong one.

Reader 2's 'What was it that made that bang?' is correct, natural English and still a subject question with What and make (no did); added. Reader 1's 'What has made that loud bang?' stays rejected: one bang that is over takes the past simple (r21b-2-028, r21c-013). 'Use What and make' gives the words, not the form; the point (no did) is still the learner's.
accept: What was it that made that bang?

why: Reader 2's 'The problem could have been solved earlier.' drops 'much' from the sentence; a rewrite keeps the content, so it is not accepted. The level flag was decided in r21c-014: past modal passive is on the B1.2 passive_modals card ('Past: modal + have been + 3. form'). Start with The problem makes the form necessary without a term (6 November); the explanation uses this sentence.

Readers list no new order: 'something to eat' / 'to eat something', the fronted before-clause and 'would you like to leave before we eat something' are all accepted (r21b-3-006, r21c-016). Lower-case cards are how every order task is shown.

Both readers' 'it was built in 1932 and the bridge is still used today' puts the pronoun before its noun and stays rejected (r21-4-028, r21c-017); reader 1's other two orders leave out the card 'it'. All natural orders, with both fronted phrases, are accepted.

Readers only note that Start with The winner leads to the form; that is the rule's way to make it necessary without a term (6 November). 'by them' in both positions and the fronted On Friday are accepted (r21c-026).

Reader 1's 'had read' needs an earlier past time to look back from, and the sentence has none (the reading happens during the time off work); rejected. 'read', 'was reading', 'would read' and 'used to read' are already accepted with answer notes (r21b-4-018); the explanation uses this sentence.

As r21c-027 decided: 'had finished already' gives 'had finished already eating', not English, and 'already finished' leaves out had, which the B1.1 narrative card needs for what happened before ('Past perfect: what happened before'). 'had already finished', ''d already finished' and 'already had finished' are accepted.
